## 30 September 2026

## Circular to intermediaries

## Obtaining client consent under the Hong Kong Investor Identification Regime for the exchange-traded derivatives market (HKIDR-DM)

This circular sets out the Securities and Futures Commission's (SFC) requirements for Relevant Regulated Intermediaries (RRIs) 1   to obtain express consent from individual clients 2 as required under paragraph 5.6A(p) of the Code of Conduct 3  for the collection and transfer of their personal data 4  to the SFC and Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited (HKEX) 5 under the HKIDR-DM, which is scheduled to be launched in the second quarter of 2028. Such consent may be obtained by written and signed acknowledgement on paper, by email, other electronic means (for example, by instant messaging applications) or by phone.

## Requirements in respect of client consent

## 1) Express consent

Client consent should be obtained in an explicit form, whereby the client clearly indicates his or her agreement to the collection and transfer of his or her personal data to HKEX and the SFC for the purposes specified in the consent. Consent must not be implied from the client's conduct, silence or omission.

## 2) Explanation of consent

Before or when obtaining client consent, an RRI should explain to the client the purpose for such consent and the consequences of not providing it. The RRI should implement procedures for obtaining client consent and explaining to clients the implications of not providing such consent.

No order or trade to open new positions shall be permitted without obtaining the client's express consent under the HKIDR-DM. If an RRI is unable to obtain client consent, it must

1 RRIs refer to SFC-licensed corporations and SFC-registered institutions which are subject to the HKIDR-DM pursuant to paragraph 5.6A of the Code of Conduct.

2   For the avoidance of doubt, the requirement to obtain express client consent for the collection and transfer of the client's personal data only applies to individual clients (ie, natural person clients) but not to corporate clients. There should be no personal data collected from corporate clients.

3   Paragraph 5.6A of the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission is set out in Appendix C to the consultation conclusions on proposals to implement an investor identification regime at trading level for the exchange-traded derivatives market in Hong Kong, released by the SFC in June 2026. These additions to the Code of Conduct will be published in the Government Gazette in due course and become effective on a date consistent with the implementation timeline as set out in the consultation conclusions.

4   'Personal data' is defined under the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (Cap. 486) as 'any data - (a) relating directly or indirectly to an individual; (b) from which it is practicable for the identity of the individual to be directly or indirectly ascertained; and (c) in a form in which access to or processing of the data is practicable'.

5   In this paper, references to HKEX mean Hong Kong Futures Exchange Limited (HKFE) or The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (SEHK) as the context requires.

not submit the client's BCAN 6  or CID 7  to HKEX under the HKIDR-DM. In such circumstances, the RRI should input an order or trade only to close out the client's existing open positions (ie, the client may only place a sell order to close his or her long positions, or a buy order to close his or her short positions).

## 3) Authentication of client identity

The identity of a client from whom the consent is obtained should be properly authenticated and validated. Where there is any doubt as to the client's identity, the RRI should make further enquiries and verify through a communication channel different from the previous one.

## 4) Purposes of use and minimum content of the consent

For the HKIDR-DM, client consent must expressly cover the following purposes of use of personal data:

- (a) the disclosure and transfer of the client's personal data (including CID and BCANs) by the RRI to HKEX and the SFC in accordance with the rules and requirements of HKEX and the SFC as updated from time to time;
- (b) allowing HKEX to: (i) collect, store, process and use their personal data (including CID and BCANs) for market surveillance and monitoring purposes and enforcement of relevant HKEX rules and procedures; (ii) disclose and transfer such information to relevant regulators and law enforcement agencies in Hong Kong (including, but not limited to, the SFC) so as to facilitate the performance of their statutory functions with respect to Hong Kong's financial markets; and (iii) use such information for conducting analysis for the purposes of market oversight; and
- (c) allowing the SFC to: (i) collect, store, process and use their personal data (including CID and BCANs) for the performance of its statutory functions including monitoring, surveillance and enforcement functions with respect to Hong Kong's financial markets; and (ii) disclose and transfer such information to relevant regulators and law enforcement agencies in Hong Kong in accordance with applicable laws or regulatory requirements.

An RRI may adopt the template set out in the Annex to obtain client consent. It may also use its own version provided that all the above purposes are included.

## 5) Proper recording of consent and withdrawals of consent

6   Please refer to the definition of 'BCAN' in paragraph 5.6A(b) of the Code of Conduct. Where client consent cannot be obtained from a client, his or her orders for closing out the client's existing open positions should be tagged with a specific code representing the BCAN in such cases in accordance with the Information Paper on HKIDR-DM released by HKEX.

7   Please refer to the definition of 'CID' in paragraph 5.6A(b) of the Code of Conduct.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

An RRI should retain the records of all client consent and withdrawals of consent, irrespective of the means by which they are provided (such as by phone or electronic means).

Where a consent or withdrawal is provided in writing, the RRI should retain relevant records, including the date on which the consent or withdrawal was provided.

For consent or withdrawals provided verbally, through email or other electronic channels (such as instant messaging applications), the RRI should retain the corresponding phone or electronic record, including the date on which the consent or withdrawal was provided.

An RRI should also maintain a written log of all client consent and withdrawals of consent, containing at least the following particulars:

- (a) the name of the client providing the consent or withdrawal;
- (b) the date on which the consent or withdrawal was provided; and
- (c) the means by which the consent or withdrawal was provided.

## 6) Maintenance of records

An RRI should retain records of all client consent and withdrawals of consent, together with the corresponding logs, for as long as the relevant person remains a client of the RRI and for a period of not less than two years after the person ceases to be a client of the RRI.

Such records and logs should be centrally maintained and stored in a secure manner that protects them against unauthorised, accidental or inappropriate access, modification, deletion or loss, and allows them to be readily accessible for compliance monitoring and audit purposes. Where phone or electronic records are retained, an RRI should have appropriate arrangements and sufficient capability to store and back up such records.

An RRI should, upon request, provide the SFC with access to, or copies of, such records and logs.

## Reliance on existing client consent

An RRI is not required to obtain new consent from an individual client for the purpose of the HKIDR-DM if both of the following conditions are met: (i) express consent has already been obtained from the client for the use of his or her personal data collected by the RRI; and (ii) such consent expressly includes all the purposes of use set out in sub-paragraphs (a) to (c) of paragraph 4 above. The consent need not reproduce those purposes verbatim, provided that all such purposes are clearly covered. For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement will not be satisfied where the purposes of use can only be implied or inferred from the consent.

Where either of the above conditions is not met, the RRI must obtain new express consent from the client either: (i) in a form that expressly covers all the purposes of use set out in sub-paragraphs (a) to (c) of paragraph 4 above; or (ii) using the template set out in the Annex to this circular.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

This circular should not be regarded as legal advice on compliance with the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance or any other applicable data privacy laws. RRIs subject to the HKIDRDM should, where necessary, seek professional advice on appropriate measures to be taken to ensure compliance with all applicable data privacy laws.
